evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（香港中文大學）
evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨、金文、戰國簡帛用例；《說文》
evidence.text: The entry reads oracle-bone 乍 as clearing vegetation, citing 乙8502; it also cites 乍（作）邑 in 合集13509 for building a settlement. It reports bronze-inscription examples for casting a ritual vessel, building a fief, making law, and serving as a standard, and Warring States bamboo-slip examples for ‘serve as’ and ‘suddenly/temporarily.’ The entry proposes that 人 was added to 乍 when the latter was used for sudden or temporary meanings, to distinguish the work/action graph 作. The same page records the Shuowen gloss 止也 for 乍; this is the database’s paleographic analysis and sense sequence, not a chronology established by a gloss list.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭 乍

evidence.source: 說文解字 online text with 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.field: 作; headword, gloss and graphic analysis
evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry gives 作 as 起也 and says 从人从乍. Duan Yucai’s commentary explicitly analyzes it as 从人，乍聲. The Shuowen gloss is a historical lexicographic statement, not direct proof of 作’s earliest attested sense or the date of its graphic formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「作」

evidence.source: 王子揚, “卜辭‘■不既作’試解,” 出土文獻（第三輯）, Tsinghua University-hosted PDF
evidence.field: Oracle-bone readings; proposed and disputed graphic relationships; sound component
evidence.text: The author reviews 曾憲通’s proposal that an oracle-bone graph was the original graph of 作, showing a person using a hand-held implement to turn soil, and rejects that specific identification and interpretation as insufficiently supported. The author separately argues that 乍（作） functions as a sound component in another oracle-bone graph, adducing graphic comparisons and examples; this concerns a sound component inside that graph, not proof that 乍’s depicted object had a recoverable name or pronunciation. The article reads 作 in the discussed divination phrase as ‘arise/recover.’ It documents a disputed oracle-bone reading rather than a settled account of all early 作 forms.
evidence.title: 卜辭“■不既作”試解

evidence.text: The page calls 乍 the original graph of 作 and interprets the oracle form as an upper-garment lapel, associated with making clothing, with 人 later added to make 作. This conflicts with the CUHK entry’s vegetation-clearing analysis. The opened text lists script categories but did not provide verified dates or individual witnesses in the inspected passage; this ancestor account is reported as the database’s proposal, not as established chronology. The site’s character database marks its materials ‘All Rights Reserved,’ so it is cited as textual evidence, not selected as an image source.
evidence.title: 漢字「乍」：字形演變

evidence.text: The inspected description identifies 乍-seal.svg as a vector depiction of 乍 in Shuowen seal-script style and links the example to the s09434 image in Hanziyuan’s 乍 data. This is a modern vector drawing of a historical script form, not an ancient artifact photograph. The description page indicates that the file is available under its specified license; the specific image is in the public-domain ancient-script category. Its file page provides the original image URL used below.

evidence.field: 乍; Baxter–Sagart 2014 MC and OC rows
evidence.text: The exact local sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv row for 乍 gives modern Mandarin zhà, MC dzraeH, OC *[dz]ˤrak-s, gloss ‘suddenly.’ This is the provided local table row, not independent proof of a sound role. Its notation differs from the 作 rows: voiced [dz] and -rak-s for this 乍 sense versus voiceless [ts] and -ak or -ak-s for 作. The retrieved evidence does not establish the sound change connecting these readings. A public table page was not successfully inspected in this pass, so the local row is not presented as externally verified table content.

search_audit.query: 作 oracle-bone reading 乍 phonetic component disputed identification Tsinghua 出土文獻 PDF
search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected the Tsinghua-hosted article; it rejects one proposal identifying a discussed oracle graph as an early 作 shape and separately argues that 乍 functions as a sound component in another graph.

gaps: Shuowen.org page opened but returned no readable body text in this pass; the quoted Shuowen entry is supported by the dossier’s prior cited transcription and not newly verified in page contents here.

The primary paleographic dispute over 乍’s pictured object remains unresolved: CUHK analyzes vegetation clearing, while Academia Sinica proposes a garment lapel. Neither inspected page establishes the name or pronunciation of any depicted object.
The Tsinghua article addresses a disputed oracle-bone graph and a separate 乍 sound-component analysis; it does not settle the origin or full graphic history of 作.

No earliest attestation date for the cited oracle, bronze, or Warring States examples was established in the inspected CUHK entry. The cited artifact/catalog identifiers are retained without inferred dates.

For a whole-graph borrowing claim based on the name of a depicted tool or object, the object’s ancient name and pronunciation remain unverified. The current materials instead support separate written uses of 乍 and 作; they do not establish such a phonetic loan mechanism.

The exact local Unihan rows confirm zhà for 乍 and zuò for 作, but official per-character endpoints could not be inspected as required click-through citations. These modern readings are metadata and do not prove an ancient sound relationship.

The exact Wikimedia Commons description pages for ACC-s05788.svg and ACC-s09434.svg were not inspectable, so only the verified 乍-seal.svg candidate is proposed. No tracked extract is recommended: reuse permission for bulk dictionary text was not verified and concise page citations suffice.

It illustrates a later conventional graph form without presenting the drawing as an ancient object photograph.
